note: Bosnia was conquered by Mehmed II in 1463 in a rapid 8-day campaign. King Stephen Tomašević — who had just refused to pay tribute — was captured and beheaded. The speed of the conquest shocked European observers; Bosnia had briefly appealed for Western help that never arrived. Many Bosnian nobility converted to Islam to retain their estates — creating the Bosnian Muslim community that persists to the present day. Herzegovina (under Stjepan Vukčić Kosača) held out until 1482.

_quarry.structural_significance: Brings Ottomans to the Adriatic coast; creates the Bosnian Muslim community through mass nobility conversion; the conversion pattern produces the ethnic and religious complexity that defines the region into the modern era
